title: Radon-measure compactness, convergence of restrictions, and a measurable slice-mass majorant (T1, T2, MM)
statement: (T1) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open and μ_j are Borel measures on ℝ^P with sup_j μ_j(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and a Borel measure μ with μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, ∫ f dμ_{φ(j)} → ∫ f dμ for every continuous f with compact support in U, limsup_j μ_{φ(j)}(K) ≤ μ(K) for compact K ⊆ U and μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_{φ(j)}(G) for open G ⊆ U. (T2) Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, X_j ⇀ X in 𝒟_k(U), (μ_j, ξ_j) admissible representations of X_j and (μ_X, ξ_X) of X (Borel measures finite on compact subsets of U; a.e. strongly measurable k-vector fields with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.; X_j(ω) = ∫ξ_j(ω)dμ_j and X(ω) = ∫ξ_X(ω)dμ_X on 𝒟^k(U)), μ a Borel measure finite on compact subsets of U with limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ U, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous and t ∈ ℝ with μ{f = t} = 0. Then ∫_{f<t} ξ_j(ω) dμ_j → ∫_{f<t} ξ_X(ω) dμ_X for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). (MM) Let μ_j be Borel measures on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, G ⊆ ℝ^P, a, b ∈ ℝ, L ∈ ℝ≥0, with μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞ for all j, and Z_j : ℝ → [0, ∞] with Z_j(t) ≤ L · liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for all j and t ∈ (a, b). Then there is a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (a, b) and ∫_{(a,b)} g dL¹ ≤ L · liminf_j μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}).
